questions.q: How was Ethereum's own development actually funded, per this lesson?
options: A public initial coin offering (ICO) that raised over 31,531 BTC
A single venture capital round
Government grants
It has never been funded — development is unpaid
questions.explain: The Ethereum Foundation ran a 42-day public ICO in 2014, creating 60 million ETH for sale and raising the equivalent of over $18 million in Bitcoin.

questions.q: What consensus mechanism did Ethereum run on at its 2015 Frontier launch?
options: Proof of work, the same as Bitcoin at the time
Proof of stake
No consensus mechanism was needed at launch
A hybrid mechanism unique to Ethereum from day one
questions.explain: Ethereum launched on proof of work like Bitcoin; the switch to proof of stake didn't happen until years later, with the 2022 Merge.

questions.q: In the API analogy used in this lesson, what does the restaurant menu represent?
options: The set of requests you can make to a piece of software, without needing to know how it works internally
The software's source code
A list of every developer who built the software
The blockchain's transaction history
questions.explain: An API is like a menu: you specify what you want, and the system (the kitchen) handles it — you don't need to understand the internal implementation.

questions.q: What is an EIP, and what real stage means it has been adopted into the protocol?
options: An Ethereum Improvement Proposal — reaching "Final" means it's adopted
A type of Ethereum wallet — reaching "Draft" means it's adopted
A mining reward — reaching "Review" means it's adopted
A smart contract template with no formal adoption process
questions.explain: An EIP moves through Idea, Draft, Review, and Last Call before reaching Final — the stage at which it's actually adopted into Ethereum's protocol.

questions.q: What real change did the Homestead upgrade (March 2016) bring to Ethereum?
options: A graphical user interface, plus formal support for future EIP-based upgrades
The transition to proof of stake
The Ethereum ETF launch
The Genesis block
questions.explain: Homestead gave Ethereum a GUI for the first time, making it usable by non-technical people, and enabled the network to run future EIP-based upgrades.
